title: Fabrication of PDMS Microfluidic Chip Device
author: Nevena Milivojević Dimitrijević

steps.title: Design microfluidic features in CAD
steps.instruction: Use SolidWorks® Premium 2022 SP0.0 to design chambers and channels, precisely delineating geometry to reproduce the desired biological event or microenvironment.

steps.title: Export and slice model for photomasks
steps.instruction: Export the CAD model as an STL file, import the STL into CHITUBOX 64, and slice the model to generate a series of 2‑D photomasks.

substeps.instruction: Export the designed model to STL format.
Open the STL file in CHITUBOX 64.
Slice the model to create 2‑D photomasks.

steps.title: 3D print photomask master
steps.instruction: Transfer the STL file via USB flash drive to the Creality LD 006 UV‑LCD stereolithography printer, set printing parameters (XY precision 50 µm, layer height 10 µm), and print the master layer‑by‑layer with resin irradiated from below according to the photomask; the printed layers remain on the upper receiving print head.

substeps.instruction: Copy the STL file to a USB flash drive.
Insert the USB drive into the Creality LD 006 printer.
Configure printer settings: XY precision 50 µm, layer height 10 µm.
Start the UV‑LCD stereolithography print.

steps.title: Post‑print cleaning and UV curing
steps.instruction: Rinse the printed substrate with isopropyl alcohol to remove non‑developed regions, irradiate the mold in a UV chamber to complete polymerization, rinse again with isopropyl alcohol, and dry with a gentle nitrogen flow.

substeps.instruction: Rinse the printed substrate with isopropyl alcohol.
Place the mold in a UV chamber for post‑irradiation.
Rinse the mold again with isopropyl alcohol.
Dry the mold using a gentle flow of nitrogen.

steps.title: Cast PDMS replica on master
steps.instruction: Mix PDMS pre‑polymer and cross‑linker at a 10:1 ratio (w/w or v/v), pour the mixture over the mold, degas in a vacuum chamber to remove bubbles and improve feature contact, then cure in an oven at 70 °C for at least 4 hours.

substeps.instruction: Mix PDMS pre‑polymer and cross‑linker in a 10:1 ratio.
Pour the PDMS mixture over the cleaned mold.
Place the assembly in a vacuum chamber to degas.
Cure the PDMS in an oven at 70 °C for a minimum of 4 hours.

steps.title: Demold, cut, and drill PDMS chip
steps.instruction: After curing, gently peel off the PDMS replica, cut it to the desired size and shape, and drill inlet and outlet holes for tube connections.

substeps.instruction: Peel the cured PDMS replica from the master mold.
Cut the PDMS piece to the required dimensions.
Drill inlet and outlet holes for tubing.

steps.title: Bond chip and establish flow
steps.instruction: Bond the PDMS chip to another PDMS replica or to a standard microscopy glass slide using controlled UV and ozone radiation, then connect the device to a peristaltic pump to establish a defined flow.

substeps.instruction: Expose the bonding surfaces to controlled UV and ozone radiation.
Press the PDMS chip onto the target surface (PDMS or glass) to complete bonding.
Connect the inlet/outlet to a peristaltic pump and set the desired flow rate.
